clue.text: Go through flames, shooting on both sides

parts.note: to go through or over something is to cross it
flames are fire

explanation.surface: A daring dash through a blaze while guns go off on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossfire is gunfire coming from two or more directions at once, catching anyone between the lines.

clue.text: Genuinely improve, absorbing energy

indicators.note: absorbing means the word for improve takes the energy letter inside itself

parts.note: to rally is to recover or improve
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone sincerely gets better by soaking up some vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: RALLY absorbs E after its first letter, giving RE-ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs of sincerity: done truly, in fact rather than in pretence.

clue.text: Seat is free for the rest of the day

indicators.note: free signals the letters of seat is are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vacant seat is available for whoever wants to lounge away the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' turns SEATIS into the answer; 'for the' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is a nap or rest taken after lunch, in the middle of the day.

clue.text: Overcharge for coat

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper asks far too much for a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece is slang for swindling someone out of money; a fleece is also a warm zip-up jacket or a sheep's woolly coat.

clue.text: Say again the others had dinner

parts.note: the rest means the others, the remainder
ate is the past tense of eat, as in had dinner

explanation.surface: Someone repeats that everyone else has already eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate is to repeat or express something once more in words.

clue.text: Baptismal offering provided by mean characters

parts.note: given can mean provided, as in given that

indicators.note: characters here means the letters of mean taken as loose characters and rearranged

explanation.surface: A christening gift supplied by some stingy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' treats the letters of 'mean' as building blocks to be rearranged into NAME; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename is bestowed at a christening, so it is what a baptism offers the child.

clue.text: Hide stone, being a miser

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
flint is a hard grey stone

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted person hides away a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being a' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a stingy person who hates spending money, as if he would skin a flint to save it.

clue.text: Islander's brother thought to bring hen round

indicators.note: hen round means the hen letters go around the other pieces

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: An islander's brother had the idea of bringing a hen over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring hen round' wraps the hen around the other pieces; the 's is read as 'is', a link. The Hebrides are islands off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebridean is a native of the Hebrides, the island chains off western Scotland.

clue.text: Relish one's plight

explanation.surface: A person enjoys their own predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish covers a sharp preserved condiment such as chutney; a plight is a difficult mess or tight spot.

clue.text: Do feel one has to be understood

parts.note: to do can mean to make, as in do or make a meal
a sense is a feeling one has, such as a sense of danger

explanation.surface: Someone does feel they need to get their point across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is comprehensible or logical is said to hang together and be clear.

clue.text: One tending to be less fat

explanation.surface: Someone who is inclined to be slimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaner is one who leans or inclines; leaner is also the comparative of lean, meaning thinner.

clue.text: Underworld boss caught traitor, a tycoon

parts.note: Pluto is the Roman god who ruled the underworld
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: A gang leader catches an informer who turns out to be a business magnate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a mobster, but it is the Roman god of the dead; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is someone whose power comes from great wealth, as a tycoon's does.

clue.text: Used line that was biased

explanation.surface: Someone fished with rod and reel, and was slanted in their views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that was' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Angled means fished with a rod and line; it also means slanted, presented with a bias.

clue.text: Look better, taking in one's make up

indicators.note: taking in means the letters for one's go inside the word for look better

parts.note: to improve is to get better, as things look better
one is I, and the possessive 's stands for is, so one's gives I and S

explanation.surface: Someone tries to look better by applying make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' is the container signal. 'make up' looks like cosmetics but means invent on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to invent or perform something on the spur of the moment, unprepared.

clue.text: Down under needing repair, so painted

indicators.note: needing repair says the letters of so painted are broken and must be put back together differently

explanation.surface: Something in Australia is in bad shape, so it has been painted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing repair' rearranges SOPAINTED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes is a name for Australia and New Zealand, on the opposite side of the globe from Britain, popularly called Down Under.

clue.text: Statement of one's aims — a clear round

parts.note: manifest means clear or obvious
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A party sets out its goals, a clear and well-rounded plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a public declaration of policy and intentions, typically by a political party.

clue.text: This boy has a range of knowledge

explanation.surface: A lad who knows a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken is a boy's name; ken is also one's scope of understanding, as in beyond my ken.

clue.text: Very important little island in Florida

explanation.surface: A small Florida islet that matters a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Key means crucial; a key is also a low island or reef, like those in the Florida Keys.

clue.text: Fall asleep over kitchen pot

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word for kitchen pot is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot used in the kitchen

explanation.surface: Someone nods off beside a pan on the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: To nap is to doze or have a short sleep.

clue.text: Ordinary criminal unnamed

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of unnamed are wrongly or lawlessly arranged

explanation.surface: A run-of-the-mill crook whose identity is unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like the noun of the surface but is the anagram signal on UNNAMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Mundane means commonplace, dull and everyday.

clue.text: Country where people burst into song

indicators.note: burst into says the people word breaks into the middle of the song word

parts.note: an aria is a song for solo voice in opera
men means people

explanation.surface: A nation where folk suddenly start singing.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN bursts into AR-IA; 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the Caucasus, between Turkey and Azerbaijan.

clue.text: Pay back for foolish chatter

indicators.note: back says the word pay is read backwards

explanation.surface: Settling a debt in return for idle talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yap is slang for silly, noisy talk, like a small dog's yapping.

clue.text: A pondering, that's funny

parts.note: musing means pondering, thinking deeply

explanation.surface: A thought that strikes someone as comical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing means entertaining, causing laughter.

clue.text: Growing endless fruit

indicators.note: endless says the word for growing loses its final letter

parts.note: raising means growing, as in raising crops

explanation.surface: A fruit that keeps on growing without limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, eaten as a dried fruit.

clue.text: Fine, not so new, document case

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
older means less new

explanation.surface: A tidy, rather aged briefcase for papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A folder is a folding cover or wallet for holding loose papers.

clue.text: Being monarch, making request

parts.note: as can mean being, as in as he was late
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: Being a ruler, someone puts in a petition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking means putting a question or making a request.

clue.text: Becoming fairly good

explanation.surface: Something both suitable and reasonably satisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent means seemly or appropriate, as becoming does; it also means satisfactory, of acceptable quality.

clue.text: Wrong-footed in disagreement?

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles while at odds with others.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of step means marching on the wrong foot, and figuratively at odds or not in harmony with others.

clue.text: Flower-love it madly

indicators.note: madly signals the letters of love it are thrown into a wild new order

explanation.surface: A gardener is crazy about a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges LOVEIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A violet is a small plant with purple blooms.

clue.text: Old musician who had verminous followers

definitions.text: Old musician who had verminous followers

parts.words: Old musician who had verminous followers
parts.note: the legendary piper of Hamelin who rid the town of rats by luring them away with his music

explanation.surface: A musician of legend trailed by a swarm of rats.
explanation.walkthrough: In the folk tale the piper in his multicoloured coat charmed the town's rats into the river, then led away its children.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary piper of Hamelin wore a coat of many colours and led the rats away with his tune.

clue.text: Passion seen in quiet case

indicators.note: seen in means the passion word appears inside the letters for quiet

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
heat means passion, intensity of feeling

explanation.surface: Ardour displayed in a hushed courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover or case, as for a sword blade.

clue.text: It helps make concrete mass

explanation.surface: Something that firms up a whole lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregate is the sand and gravel mixed with cement into concrete; it also means a total or collected whole.
